Situation1: Their partner faces a tough decision at work and seeks advice and encouragement.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Story: I was sitting on the couch, holding my partner’s hand as they stared anxiously at their laptop. They’d just received an email about a major project at work, and the decision they had to make could change everything. “I just need you to listen,” they said, voice trembling. I nodded, trying to be present, offering the comfort and encouragement they needed. My phone buzzed. It was my friend, panicked. “I think I left my passport at home! My flight’s in two hours—can you check and bring it to the airport if it’s here?” I could hear the desperation in their voice. My partner squeezed my hand, eyes pleading for support, while my friend waited on the line, hoping I’d drop everything to help. I felt torn, my heart racing as I weighed the expectations pressing in from both sides. I wanted to be there for both of them, but I knew I couldn’t be in two places at once.
